guard: Ctrl-C on a foreground `cotal up` follows the same sparing rule as bare `cotal down` (#1307): the seat snapshot is taken while the manager still answers, the exact recorded manager's spare capability is asserted before any signal, the teardown is awaited before the broker is signalled, and the seats left behind are reported with the reap route. The handler is idempotent under a second Ctrl-C.
why: The suite drives the shipped foreground `up` as a real subprocess with a real managed seat (a shim
`claude` on PATH resolving to a real core-dist mesh endpoint), so a mutant that arms the destructive
intent is observed as a DEAD SEAT PROCESS, not inferred from a source string.
M1 (arm the intent) is the destructive regression this guard exists for. A bare arm is refused by
the shipped reservation gate, so the mutant writes the stop reservation itself before arming; the
manager consumes a valid intent and reaps every managed seat. The seat-survives cell is the named
assertion; the throw aborts the section before the report cell could add a second red.
M2 (remove the spared report) restores the pre-fix silence: the stack still tears down and the seat
still survives, but the operator is told nothing. Only the spared-report cell can notice, which is
why it is the named assertion.
Both mutations run the CLI as a subprocess, so they mutate a module only `dist/` delivers to it:
every mutation builds first and rebuilds in `afterRestore` (dist/ is gitignored; git cannot be the
recovery for a build compiled from the mutant).

mutations.name: M1 the handler arms the destructive shutdown intent with its own reservation, so the manager reaps every managed seat on Ctrl-C
mutations.expectRed: the seat SURVIVES the Ctrl-C teardown
mutations.cell: the seat SURVIVES the Ctrl-C teardown
mutations.note: The destructive shape #1307 guards against: the foreground handler publishing the one-shot with-agents intent before signalling the manager. A bare arm is refused by the shipped gate (it requires the stop reservation only cotal down's stopLocalProcess holds) and grades WRONG-RED on the refusal, so the mutant creates the reservation itself first, exactly as the destructive regression would have to. The manager's signal handler then consumes a valid v1 intent and mgr.stop({ withAgents: true }) reaps the seat, so the first cell that can notice is the seat-survives cell; the report cell would also red on the empty snapshot but the throw aborts the section first. Deterministic: the reservation write, the arm and the consume all succeed on every run.

mutations.name: M2 the handler stops reporting the seats it left behind
mutations.expectRed: the spared report names the seat and the reap route
mutations.cell: the spared report names the seat and the reap route
mutations.note: The pre-fix silence: teardown still works and the seat still survives, but the operator is told nothing about live work while bare `down` reports it. Only the spared-report cell can notice, so it is the named assertion; the snapshot is still taken, so no earlier cell moves.
